summary: Japan is cash-friendlier than most developed countries, but card acceptance in Tokyo has risen sharply since 2020. IC cards (Suica / PASMO) tap-to-pay at almost every train, bus, and convenience store, and Apple Pay with a Suica in your Wallet is the smoothest tourist setup.

methods.label: Cash (JPY)
methods.notes: Still the only option at many small izakaya, family-run ramen shops, temples, and rural inns.

methods.label: Suica / PASMO (IC card)
methods.notes: Transit everywhere; also taps at 7-Eleven, Family Mart, Lawson, most vending machines, and many restaurants.

methods.label: Visa credit / debit
methods.notes: Most hotels, chains, and department stores. Tap-to-pay is rolling out fast.

methods.label: American Express
methods.notes: Hotels and big department stores yes; small shops often not.

methods.label: JCB
methods.notes: Domestic card brand — widely accepted. Discover + Diners can piggyback on JCB acceptance.

methods.label: Apple Pay (with Suica or Visa)
methods.notes: If your iPhone Wallet has a Suica, you get the broadest coverage; Apple Pay with a Visa works at card-enabled terminals only.

methods.label: Google Pay
methods.notes: Tap-to-pay only works where the card network is tap-enabled — still narrower than Suica.

methods.label: PayPay (QR)
methods.notes: Dominant domestic QR-pay. You can load funds with an international card but most tourists skip it.

methods.label: Alipay / WeChat Pay
methods.notes: Common at shops courting Chinese tourists, especially around Ginza and Shinjuku.

methods.label: Wise / Revolut card
methods.notes: Works anywhere Visa/Mastercard is accepted; often the cheapest FX.

atm_notes: 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) ATMs accept Visa/Mastercard/Amex/UnionPay from foreign cards and have an English menu — there's one in most konbini. Japan Post ATMs also work. Most other ATMs reject foreign cards. Daily withdrawal limits are often set by your home bank, not the ATM.
tax_refund_note: Visitors on a short-stay visa can shop tax-free at stores displaying the 'Japan. Tax-free Shop' sign, with a minimum ¥5,500 per store per day. Bring your passport. From 2026 the system moves to a refund-on-departure model — check the latest process at the airport.
